newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-THREE RACES SCHEDULED FOR SATURDAY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-THREE RACES SCHEDULED FOR SATURDAY.

text.p: The last day of the Alpine skiing world championships on Saturday will be crowded with three medal races and some of the women having to compete twice within the space of a few hours.
Organisers said the women's combined downhill, which was called off on Thursday and Friday due to bad weather, would be held at 1200 GMT on Saturday.
Before that, the regular women's downhill will be held at 0930 GMT. The men's slalom at 1700 and 2000 will then be the final event before the closing ceremonies.
The re-scheduling is likely to affect the German women skiers Katja Seizinger and Hilde Gerg most of all. There are only 19 starters in the combined downhill.
Seizinger is the 1994 Olympic downhill champion and a frontrunner for the world title. She is also well placed with Gerg, another good downhiller, for the combined title.
It will not be the first time this season that the women have had two speed races in a day however.
On December 7 in Vail, they held a World Cup super-giant slalom and then hours later the downhill.
Two women's downhills were also scheduled for the same day in Bad Kleinkirchheim, Austria, in January because of bad weather but only one was eventually staged.

The decision to postpone Friday's race was made after officials had already delayed the start an hour because of wind and snow, which began falling overnight and dumped several centimetres on the Kandahar piste.
The weather improved considerably later in the day but much work needed to be done in preparing the piste.
Organisers had said earlier that the postponement could, in a worst case scenario, extend the championships to Sunday or Monday although that would cause major problems.
The slalom leg of the combined was held on Thursday night. Italy's Morena Gallizio was the fastest in that.
